title: CLI entry guard exits 0 silently when the script is reached through a symlinked directory (npm test fails on macOS)
description:
Found 2026-09-19 while re-verifying the cloud runs' work: `npm test` on macOS is 107/108. The failing test is `scripts/validate-datapackage.test.mjs:45` ("the CLI reports and exits 1 even when its own path contains a space"). The cloud runs (Linux) reported 108/108, so it only shows where a temp dir or checkout path goes through a symlink.

Cause: the CLI entry guard `process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` compares a realpath'd URL (Node resolves symlinks for import.meta.url) with a URL built from the raw argv path (symlinks preserved). Reached through a symlinked directory the guard is false and the CLI prints nothing and exits 0, on a package with real errors. This is the same silent-exit-0 defect the guard was written to fix, still present for symlinks. On macOS os.tmpdir() (/var/folders/... -> /private/var/...) and /tmp are symlinks, so the test trips it.

Reproduce: copy scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs to /private/tmp/x/'real dir'/v.mjs, symlink /private/tmp/x/linkdir -> that directory, then `node /private/tmp/x/linkdir/v.mjs scripts/fixtures/bad-name`: exit 0 through the symlink, exit 1 via the real path. `scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs` has the identical guard and the identical failure (verified: exit 1 via real path, exit 0 via symlink).

Files: scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs and its two byte-identical copies datasets/climate-and-environment/co2-ppm/scripts/ and datasets/energy-and-commodities/oil-prices/scripts/ (keep all three identical), scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs, and their tests. Likely fix: compare realpathSync(process.argv[1]) to fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), keeping the bare-import guard on process.argv[1]. Add a test that reaches the CLI through an explicitly created symlink so it does not depend on the platform's tmpdir. Do not linewrap Markdown.
notes: 2026-09-19 fixed. Changed: scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs (and its two byte-identical copies in co2-ppm/scripts and oil-prices/scripts, md5 checked), scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs, and tests scripts/validate-datapackage.test.mjs and scripts/check-invisible-characters.test.mjs. Fix: the entry-point guard now compares import.meta.url with pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href inside a try/catch (realpathSync throws for the undefined argv[1] of node -e and for a missing path, both meaning imported-not-run), replacing the raw-argv comparison. TDD: added a symlinked-directory CLI test for each script (explicit symlinkSync, so they do not depend on the platform tmpdir); before the fix 3 tests failed (both new ones and the existing space test, on macOS), after it all pass. Results: npm test 146/146 (needed npm install in datasets/climate-and-environment/us-natural-hazard-statistics first, the documented per-dataset step), npm run check:invisible clean, validator 0 errors and 0 warnings on all six datasets. Manual edge cases all correct: real path with a non-ASCII and spaced directory, symlink to the file, symlink to the directory, relative path, valid package exits 0, bare import does not run the CLI, invisible check via symlinked directory exits 1. Not done here: an independent review agent (change is a few lines per file, verified by the edge cases above).

title: Tesla worked example: autonomous source discovery, scraping and reproducible quarterly data
description:
Read AGENTS.md, NEXT.md, docs/next-session-brief.md and parent datapressr-03u. This is an end-to-end worked example of an agent starting with a data question, finding suitable sources, scraping them and producing a reproducible dataset with little human direction. The original question is Tesla quarterly sales/deliveries by vehicle over time; source reporting may only support grouped models and some periods. Do not promise finer granularity than the evidence.

Files owned: datasets/transport/tesla-quarterly-deliveries/{AGENTS.md,README.md,datapackage.json,.datahubignore,fetch.ts,build.ts,build.test.mjs,archive/,data/}; optional local package.json/package-lock.json only for a necessary parser; docs/examples/tesla-source-discovery.md. This is one dataset, not an entire Tesla portal/catalog. Do not create a new external repo or publication in this task.

1. Source discovery: start from official Tesla investor-relations quarterly releases, shareholder updates and filings; follow links from official indexes. Verify exact current URLs during execution. Use primary-source copies of historical documents when needed. Compare secondary aggregators only to find gaps or corroborate, never silently substitute estimates. Record search queries, candidate URLs, accepted/rejected sources, retrieval date, reporting coverage, reported model groupings, measurement definitions and license/terms evidence. Aim for all verifiable quarters discoverable from the official archive through the latest completed quarter with a released report; pin an explicit cutoff and record earlier missing periods rather than claim completeness. Discovery budget: 60 minutes; a blocked candidate gets at most 15 minutes before trying an alternative. A documented access limit is a result, not permission to guess.

2. Decide and record the source-backed schema before scraping. Proposed long-form output: period_start (date), period_end (date), vehicle_group (string), metric (string: deliveries or the exact verified measure), vehicles (integer), source_id (string). Primary key: period_start, period_end, vehicle_group, metric. Keep production in a separate metric if included; never relabel it deliveries, and do not equate revenue with unit sales. Preserve reported combined groups verbatim or with an explicit stable mapping; do not split a combined group into individual models or sum overlapping total/component rows. Source revisions need an explicit preferred-version rule with both snapshots retained.

3. Read skills/archive/SKILL.md and skills/structure/SKILL.md. Write fetch.ts for bounded, paced retrieval with explicit timeouts, capped retries and a source manifest containing URL, source_id, retrieval timestamp, content hash, local path and reporting period. Reuse snapshots on rerun unless an explicit refresh is requested. Try plain HTTP first; if a browser is necessary, record exactly what required it and preserve the downloaded document for offline parsing. Respect access restrictions; no credentials, paid services or bypasses. Keep source volume well below the small-data ceiling.

4. Archive evidence before parsing. Record license uncertainty honestly; do not invent a redistribution license. If permissions remain unresolved, retain a stub package and the evidence report, record the blocked publication/structured status and continue useful local verification. Follow repository source/license requirements before advancing lifecycle status.

5. Write build.ts to consume only archived inputs and emit data/tesla-quarterly-deliveries.csv plus a source resource if needed, with typed metadata, primary keys, provenance links and data conventions. Use plain Node and one targeted parser only when required. Preserve true missing values and actual zeros distinctly. Report every discovered quarter as parsed or explicitly unavailable/unsupported; assert malformed tables, duplicate/conflicting keys, unexplained gaps and mismatched source totals rather than silently dropping them.

6. Test extraction against archived fixtures spanning at least two reporting layouts/grouping regimes where available. Assert known source numbers, comma-separated integers, missing vs zero, duplicate/revised quarters and grouped-model behavior. Independently spot-check earliest/latest available quarters plus one grouping change and one revision/exception if present. Rebuild twice without network and compare output hashes. Run node scripts/validate-datapackage.mjs datasets/transport/tesla-quarterly-deliveries and npm test from root.

7. Write docs/examples/tesla-source-discovery.md as a concise walkthrough with runnable fetch/build commands, source-selection rationale, coverage/gaps table, evidence-backed sample results and an autonomy log: decisions made unaided, failed approaches, human interventions (including zero), elapsed time and tools used. State what this example teaches beyond archive/structure, and list concrete follow-up suggestions without inventing a generic scraping framework. README covers definitions, coverage, revisions, license limitations and rerun instructions.

title: Detect silent source revisions: a shared fetch --refresh and manifest-hash diff helper
description:
Nothing in this repo detects that a source has silently revised a snapshot. Evidence from the second discovery rep: the NWS PDFs carry a `Report generated:` date showing old years were regenerated without notice (2007-2015 all in 2016, 2019 in 2021, 2024 in 2026), and the Tesla releases restate figures without reissuing. With no index there is also no change feed, so re-fetching and diffing is the only way to see it.

Proposed: a shared helper (not a per-dataset habit) that runs a dataset's `fetch.ts --refresh` into a scratch directory and diffs content hashes against the committed archive/manifest.json, reporting which sources changed and by how much, without touching archive/. It would suit any `monitored` dataset. Start by reading the two existing fetch.ts implementations (tesla-quarterly-deliveries, us-natural-hazard-statistics) and extracting only what they already share; do not invent a generic scraping framework. Acceptance: one command per dataset that exits non-zero when a source changed, with a fixture-based test for both the changed and unchanged cases. Do not linewrap Markdown.

title: Owner decisions: four small repo-convention choices raised by cloud runs
description:
Four small convention choices surfaced by the cloud runs of 2026-09-18/19, each a real trade-off rather than a defect. Decide each and record it here; the agent-ready follow-up is trivial once decided.

1. AGENTS.md "Missing values": add the converse clause? Proposed wording, one clause on the existing bullet: "...Don't mix NA, N/A, -, 0, and empty string for 'missing' within one column, and note the converse: where a literal NA is a real code (North America, Namibia), keep it verbatim and say so in the field description." The skills/structure "Values that lie" block (datapressr-eec) already says this; AGENTS.md was left untouched because the Bead made it conditional on the owner.
2. Worked-example paths in skills/: the four in-repo ones (co2-ppm, oil-prices, population-growth, airports) are repo-relative, so they are clickable in the repo and dead for anyone who installed the skill with `npx skills add datasets/datapressr`. Make them absolute (works everywhere) or keep relative (clickable here)?
3. Per-dataset AGENTS.md copies: currently byte-identical to the root file, which carries repo-level task-tracking (Beads) instructions a dataset that becomes its own repo does not need. Keep byte-identical, or make the copies a dataset-relevant subset? The two rules pull opposite ways.
4. changelog/2026-09-18-tesla-quarterly-deliveries.md covers the Tesla dataset and two structure-skill sections together. Split the skill guidance into its own entry?
notes: 2026-09-19 (from the second cloud run): fifth choice. The adversarial-review step, where a fresh reviewer independently re-derives the numbers and tries to break the build, is a convention of the cloud runs, not a rule in any document. In both source-discovery reps the single most valuable finding came from it (rep 1's wrong coverage rows; rep 2's two latent silent-failure paths). docs/source-discovery-playbook.md says so in its limitations, but neither it nor skills/structure/SKILL.md requires it. title: Extend the invisible-character check to .json and .yaml with a rule that spares archive/ and data/
description:
scripts/check-invisible-characters.mjs (commits 4106152, fbd5cdf) checks nine source extensions (.ts .mts .cts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .jsx .py) and never anything under archive/. `.json` and `.yaml` are named gaps in its header. A stray U+00A0 pasted into a hand-written datapackage.json field description would not be caught, nor would one in a CI `run:` block if the repo grows workflow files. No tracked JSON carries one today.

Closing the gap needs a rule first: separate hand-written metadata (datapackage.json, package.json, config) from `archive/` and `data/` payloads, which are records of what a source said and must never be rewritten (airports publishes U+00A0 and U+200B in place names on purpose). Write that rule, extend the scan, add a negative-control test that fails without the extension, keep the existing 25+ tests green. Do not linewrap Markdown.
